When audit log entries exist, `get_item_key` receives a datetime and raises TypeError; cursor filtering would also use the wrong type. Any privileged request with optimized_pagination=true will fail."

Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing, so this raises instead of returning rows. A crafted or malformed cursor can cause a 500 on the optimized audit-log path."

      "body": "The modified offset logic uses the raw offset for previous-page cursors, so a negative offset parsed from a user-supplied cursor is passed to QuerySet slicing. Django does not support negative offsets; this can crash any endpoint using `BasePaginator` or `DateTimePaginator`. Negative offsets should be rejected with a controlled validation error such as `BadPaginationError`."
    },

Combined with the paginator changes, invalid negative offsets reach database slicing code. Validation should reject negative offsets instead of allowing them to propagate."
    },

      "severity": "high",

      "title": "Typo prevents reversing ordering for previous-page pagination",
      "body": "In `BasePaginator.build_queryset`, when converting an existing descending order to ascending, the code assigns `queryset.query.order_b` instead of `queryset.query.order_by`. The queryset therefore keeps the descending order while the cursor logic uses ascending operators and later reverses results, which can return incorrect pages. This affects paginators inheriting from `BasePaginator`, including the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator`."

Important cases are untested: datetime ordering with `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, negative or malformed cursor offsets, permission gating of optimized pagination, and backward compatibility with existing cursors. These omissions are risky because pagination bugs can cause incorrect pages or 500 errors."

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with the datetime ordering used here
findings.body: The endpoint passes `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by=-datetime`, but `OptimizedCursorPaginator` uses numeric key extraction (`math.floor`/`math.ceil`) and does not convert cursor values to datetimes like `DateTimePaginator`. When audit log entries exist, `get_item_key` receives a datetime and raises TypeError; cursor filtering would also use the wrong type. Any privileged request with optimized_pagination=true will fail.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator attempts negative QuerySet slicing
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset` is negative, the paginator slices the Django QuerySet with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]`). Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing, so this raises instead of returning rows. A crafted or malformed cursor can cause a 500 on the optimized audit-log path.

findings.title: BasePaginator allows negative offsets for previous cursors to reach QuerySet slicing
findings.body: The modified offset logic uses the raw offset for previous-page cursors, so a negative offset parsed from a user-supplied cursor is passed to QuerySet slicing. Django does not support negative offsets; this can crash any endpoint using `BasePaginator` or `DateTimePaginator`. Negative offsets should be rejected with a controlled validation error such as `BadPaginationError`.

findings.title: Cursor accepts negative offsets without validation
findings.body: `Cursor` casts `offset` to int but does not validate that it is non-negative, and `Cursor.from_string` parses user-provided cursor strings with negative offsets. Combined with the paginator changes, invalid negative offsets reach database slicing code. Validation should reject negative offsets instead of allowing them to propagate.

findings.title: Typo prevents reversing ordering for previous-page pagination
findings.body: In `BasePaginator.build_queryset`, when converting an existing descending order to ascending, the code assigns `queryset.query.order_b` instead of `queryset.query.order_by`. The queryset therefore keeps the descending order while the cursor logic uses ascending operators and later reverses results, which can return incorrect pages. This affects paginators inheriting from `BasePaginator`, including the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator`.

findings.title: No tests for the new paginator or the endpoint's optimized path
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator class, changes core offset handling in `BasePaginator`, and conditionally switches the audit-log endpoint to the new paginator, but includes no tests. Important cases are untested: datetime ordering with `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, negative or malformed cursor offsets, permission gating of optimized pagination, and backward compatibility with existing cursors. These omissions are risky because pagination bugs can cause incorrect pages or 500 errors.
